The Active Evidence Aggregator (AEA) operates as a deterministic reduction function that transforms a hierarchical array of factor-evidence pairs into a flat, filtered list of unique source names. It employs a linear scan with constant-time set lookups to achieve O(n) time complexity, where n is the number of factors. The AEA enforces three core constraints: (1) Active Status - only items marked as 'ACTIVE' are included, effectively implementing a logical projection onto the feasible set of the optimization problem solved by the underlying model; (2) Freshness Validation - items flagged as 'MISSING' are rejected, preventing the use of out-of-date statistics that could introduce systematic errors; (3) Deduplication Filter - a hash table tracks seen identifiers, eliminating multicollinearity among explanatory variables and ensuring that each source contributes independent information. Mathematically, the AEA can be viewed as a many-to-one mapping from the space of detailed factor breakdowns to the space of compact source signatures, which preserves the ordering of importance but discards redundant detail. This construction guarantees that the resulting list is both minimal and sufficient for downstream verification tasks, thereby acting as a lossy compression tailored specifically for interpretability purposes.
